c.v: Newark Quality Roofing strips the covering to the deck, repairs the deck, builds tapered insulation to positive drainage, and installs the new membrane to manufacturer specification.

runs.v: A tear-off removes everything down to the deck, while a recover installs a new membrane over the existing roof system and is cheaper and faster because it skips most disposal; the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal when the roof is water-soaked, is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or already carries 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. Commercial roofs need proper drainage design to prevent ponding, so tapered insulation builds at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to clear the ponding water the NRCA and ARMA count as a defect after 48 hours. faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial roof replacement in Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. A commercial or multi-family roof replacement in Orange always needs a construction permit under the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; confirm filing details with the City of Orange Township construction office.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for roof repair and roof replacement in New Jersey?

runs.v: It is the permit line in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7: on a commercial or multi-family building, repairing up to 25% of the roof area in any 12-month period counts as ordinary maintenance, and work past that share needs a construction permit. The rule sets the paperwork, not the diagnosis: isolated roofing issues on a dry roof call for roof repair, while wet insulation across large areas or a membrane past its service life calls for a new roof.

faqs.q: Does a commercial roof replacement on a building in an Orange historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A building inside a historic district can need extra review for exterior roofing work, separate from the construction permit, so confirm current requirements with the City of Orange Township construction office before work begins. A National or State Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof, per the National Park Service.

faqs.q: What is the best replacement membrane for an Orange commercial building?

runs.v: It depends on the building, the drainage, and the use. TPO and EPDM are the most common choices, PVC resists rooftop grease and chemical exposure, modified bitumen handles foot traffic, and white PVC and TPO carry high solar reflectance measured per ASTM C1549; lifespans run from 7 to 20 years for TPO to about 30 years for built-up roofing, per the InterNACHI chart.

faqs.q: How does an infrared moisture survey scope an Orange roof replacement?

runs.v: An ASTM C1153 infrared moisture survey finds the wet insulation under an intact membrane, because wet insulation retains heat longer than dry insulation and reads as a warm anomaly after sunset, per ASTM and the NRCA. Core cuts verify the readings and fix the saturated area before tear-off, on Valley Arts loft roofs and Main Street commercial blocks alike.
